item.title: Chinese automakers are following Tesla’s bet that robots are the next big profit machine
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Technical progress has encouraged a new batch of companies to jump in on the promise of profits from humanoid robots. And they're all Chinese automakers.

item.title: Is the best way to watch a movie on a pair of sunglasses?
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Are XREAL's smart glasses the way of the future for home entertainment?

item.title: Neocloud Lambda secures $1B in debt to buy more chips
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: Neocloud Lambda has raised $1B in private debt to buy Nvidia AI chips and lease them to Microsoft. It's the latest in a string of loans, underscoring the high cost of the AI boom.

item.title: An Anthropic researcher just gave us a peek at self-improving AI
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: Given 10 benchmarks for specific misaligned behaviors, the automated systems were able to improve performance on every single one without degrading overall performance.

item.title: Brave’s browser one-ups Chrome with its new support for email aliases
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: The feature, announced this week, allows Brave's users to sign up for websites and other online services without having to share their personal email addresses.

item.title: Open-weight AI companies are the Valley’s hottest acquisition targets
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: There's a lot of capital pouring into the business of giving models away.

item.title: How Sweden built one of Europe’s hottest startup ecosystems
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: Sophia Bendz, general partner at Cherry Ventures, stopped by Equity to break down the latest in the Swedish tech ecosystem.

item.title: More Americans oppose police license plate cameras than support them: survey
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: The backlash against license plate readers comes amid a wave of police abuses of surveillance cameras.

item.title: Friend-focused photo-sharing app Retro snags $21M
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Retro, a friend-focused photo-sharing app built by former Instagram employees, has raised more than $21 million in Series A funding.

item.title: Apple TV is raising its subscription prices again
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: Now, Apple TV subscriptions will cost $14.99 per month, up from its previous price of $12.99 per month.

item.title: a16z creates a $1.1B ‘Machine Age’ fund to ‘accelerate the physical buildout of AI’
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: The firm, known for its focus on software, is going to start throwing more money at the hardware behind AI.

item.title: Anthropic gets its first court win over the Pentagon’s supply-chain risk label
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration illegally labeled Anthropic a supply-chain risk, handing the AI company a victory as its second Pentagon lawsuit continues in Washington.

item.title: Meta executive leaves for OpenAI as the social media giant faces growing scrutiny in India
item.dc:creator: Jagmeet Singh
item.description: Sandhya Devanathan will oversee some OpenAI operations across Southeast Asia and Australia in her new role.

item.title: As electric two-wheelers gain a foothold, Belgian startup Any bets on cargo space
item.dc:creator: Anna Heim
item.description: Launched by Belgian startup Any, LUV1 is a modular electric motorcycle with 120 liters of cargo space that can be used to carry bags, work equipment, or even pets.

item.title: AI, athletes, and Keith Rabois: StrictlyVC is back in New York on September 10
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: A boutique StrictlyVC evening returns to New York's West Village on September 10 with Keith Rabois, Craig Shapiro, Jason Levien, Tristan Walker, Brynn Putnam, and Deven Parekh — covering AI, sports investing, community-building, venture economics, and politics, with cocktails, food, and networking throughout the night.

item.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are joining the AI stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, the AI Stage is back to dig into the single hottest topic in the community for the past few years, presented by Google for Startups.

item.title: Rivian’s CFO is leaving the company
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane, Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Claire McDonough is stepping down on October 30 to pursue a new opportunity, the company said in a filing on Thursday.

item.title: Bluesky adds an ‘algorithmic opt-out’ feature for those who don’t want to go viral
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Sometimes people just want to post to their followers, Bluesky says.

item.title: Buried in Meta’s $18B settlement is a legal pass on kids’ data
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Meta’s settlement with 29 states allows it to retain certain data from children under 13 to train and test age-detection models, highlighting a privacy trade-off built into the deal.

item.title: YouTube now lets creators tag Amazon products and earn commissions from purchases
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: The update turns product recommendations into a more direct revenue stream for creators, and for Amazon, the move puts its massive online marketplace inside one of the most popular video platforms.
